competition.flat_book_pnl: A flat seat has zero net financing/competition P&L: paper NAV earning SOFR is benchmarked at SOFR, so those flows cancel, and shocked-risk financing is zero.
competition.funding_basis: Official NY Fed SOFR ACT/360 is the zero-return competition benchmark, not free alpha. Every seat has $100m paper NAV that may be described as earning SOFR, but that capital is equally funded/benchmarked at SOFR so those flows cancel. Deployed shocked-risk capital pays the same official SOFR on trusted standard-shock risk capital: the absolute MTM loss from a 1% adverse spot move, a 100bp (1 percentage point) adverse outright rate move, or a 100bp adverse curve/RV spread move. Supported STIR contracts use exchange DV01 and currency conversion; historical rows without that stamp keep the legacy duration-one vintage and are not silently restated. Equal risk capital receives equal financing treatment across asset classes. Notional is descriptive, not the funding base. A completely flat book — including no-trade-skeptic — therefore has zero net financing/competition P&L from SOFR cash or funding economics. Positive financing/carry alpha requires an explicit markable strategy that earns above SOFR or funds below SOFR. Weekends and holidays carry the last applicable published fixing until the next fixing. If official fixing history cannot be established, new funding accrual fails closed and prior canonical balances are preserved.
competition.instruction: Do not optimize for gross notional or fill available capacity. Size risk from plausible adverse paths and historical excursions while staying inside the trusted risk-capital and drawdown limits. Flat cash at SOFR is the zero benchmark, not a source of alpha. The no-trade-skeptic must include a structured funding_view on every new risk or NO_TRADE thesis: the frozen official SOFR fixing, the relevant SR3 forward-curve view, its own assessment of whether realized funding will print higher, lower, or about the same as the curve, and the implication for remaining at the zero SOFR benchmark versus paying SOFR on shocked-risk capital.
competition.objective: Finish with the highest cumulative net paper P&L across the 14 standing seats.

research_supplement.summary: Overnight markets repriced a more aggressive Federal Reserve path after October consumer prices rose 0.4 percent, more than expected. Treasury yields jumped, with the two-year at 4.73 percent and the ten-year at 4.98 percent, while December SOFR futures imply about 4.28 percent against a 3.88 percent SOFR fixing. Equities absorbed the move better than bonds: the S&P 500 is near 7521, the Nasdaq near 25066, and the VIX near 20. Commodity marks are firm, with WTI near 86 dollars, Brent near 91.50, and gold futures near 4030, after Brent only briefly traded under 90. The dollar is mixed: euro-dollar is 1.1214 and dollar-yen is near 158.2. Australian dollar-kiwi near 1.227 broke its recent range lower and remains a rich multi-year percentile. Missing non-US consumer and labor series are a research caveat, not a trading ban, and kiwi spot does not need a New Zealand yield curve. Next up are US producer prices and the euro-area GDP flash on November 13, then Canadian CPI and Japanese GDP on November 16.

perma-bull.thesis: North American growth is firm enough to keep the front-end pays. March SOFR at 4.53 still sits below June and September, while cash at 3.88 already trails the December contract at 4.28. Canada March at 2.965 still faces a February terminal near 2.77, and Australia March at 4.885 remains a small premium to 4.85 cash with Brent near 91.50. Kiwi spot near the 4th percentile is the weaker expression of the same resilience, so that long comes off and the three pays stay.
perma-bull.invalidation: The pays are wrong if the two-year gives back the 17 basis point jump and December futures converge back toward 3.88 cash.

perma-bear.thesis: The hotter inflation print repriced the two-year to 4.73 and the ten-year to 4.98, with December futures at 4.28 against cash at 3.88. That tightening can still break growth later, so a residual ten-year long from the 5.24 entry remains the defensive expression. It does not justify leaving the full line on into producer prices on 13 November after the fresh yield has already cheapened from 4.88 to 4.98. Halving the long keeps the slowdown tail and limits another inflation print.
perma-bear.invalidation: The residual long is invalidated if the ten-year yield rises back through the 5.24 entry. Restoring the cut would require producer prices to cool and the ten-year to trade back through 4.88 before the December meeting.

dollar-king.thesis: A 0.4 percent inflation print lifted the two-year to 4.73 and the ten-year to 4.98, with December futures at 4.28 against cash at 3.88. Dollar-yen at 158.18 is back through the 158.06 entry and in the 88th percentile of five years, so the existing long is the dollar spot that took the hike premium. The euro rose on the day, and dollar-Canada or the Australian dollar would each add a second central bank. The 20 million long stays.
dollar-king.invalidation: The long is invalidated if dollar-yen sustains below the 158.06 entry after the two-year has reached 4.73, or if December futures converge back toward 3.88 cash and the hike premium leaves the pair.

expression_memo.rationale: HOLD pos-012b8f0c252c keeps the decision inside the frozen marks without opening a new expression.

cross-merchant.thesis: Short Australian dollar-kiwi remains the clean non-dollar expression of a rich Australia against a cheap kiwi. Spot is 1.2266, a five-year z-score of 2.34 and the 96th percentile, after a 1.2 percent five-day decline and a close through the prior 20-session range. A fresh flat book would not reopen the full 20 million at this low, so 10 million comes off and 10 million stays while the extreme is unfinished. New Zealand yields stay research context. The spot cross is the leg.
cross-merchant.invalidation: Cover the residual if the cross reclaims the broken range and holds back through 1.2456, or if it settles through about 1.212 and the five-year richness is gone. Do not replace the residual with Australian dollar-Canada.

expression_memo.rationale: REDUCE AUDNZD keeps the decision inside the frozen marks without opening a new expression.

performance_reflections.what_happened_vs_expected: The Australian dollar-kiwi short was expected to keep paying as a multi-week fade of five-year richness without a one-session air pocket in standing. Standing slipped while the short was still onside, and the same cross later extended and made a fresh open-profit high with spot at 1.2266.
performance_reflections.no_new_lesson: The standing slip was path around an intact Australia-versus-New Zealand short that later extended, so the original process remains sound: the cross was the right expression, the closed Australia-Canada fade stays shut, and a multi-week richness book is not abandoned because standing dipped for a session.

causal.original_belief: A short Australian dollar-kiwi sized for a multi-week fade of extreme Australia-versus-New Zealand richness would pay lower without a leaderboard air pocket once the cross had already started to decline.
causal.observed_reality: Standing fell while the short was still onside, and the same short later pushed to a fresh open-profit high with spot at 1.2266, still a five-year z-score of 2.34.
causal.assumptions_right: The non-dollar cross was the right place to express rich Australia against cheap New Zealand, and the cross did break its 20-session range lower while remaining historically rich.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The path was treated as if a multi-week fade should be monotonic, underweighting ordinary back-and-forth inside a still-rich cross and the fact that a one-session standing slip does not mean the differential failed.
causal.causal_divergence: Standing moved while the instrument kept the short's direction, so the scoreboard diverged from the cross that was actually being tested.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same cross still rich and the horizon only partly elapsed, the book should have stayed short and should not have flipped into Australian dollar-Canada or covered on the standing slip.
causal.future_implication: Keep a reduced Australian dollar-kiwi short while the five-year extreme remains, and do not re-initiate the original full size at the 20-session low or reopen the closed Australia-Canada fade.

carry-is-king.thesis: The Canada March 2027 receive stays at 25 million. Cash is unchanged at 2.52 and the fresh implied rate is 2.965, still about 44 basis points over cash and below the 2.995 entry, so the book is paid to wait. The backup from the book mark is not a change in cash policy. A new US receive would fight the post-inflation path, and Australia at 4.885 versus 4.85 cash does not pay enough to re-enter.
carry-is-king.invalidation: Exit the Canada receive if cash leaves 2.52, or if the implied rate reprices persistently through the 2.995 entry by more than a small headline backup while cash policy is unchanged. Paying December futures at 4.28 against 3.88 funding is rejected because the carry is negative.

expression_memo.rationale: HOLD pos-23b8d2f30846 keeps the decision inside the frozen marks without opening a new expression.

postmortems.what_worked: Australia cash never left 4.85 and did not approach the 4.60 cash-regime invalidation, so the policy-on-hold half of the book was intact at the exit.
postmortems.what_failed: The March 2027 Australia receive was entered at 4.83, below the 4.85 cash rate, and was exited at 4.88 after a hold from early October to the prior session.
postmortems.thesis_assessment: The cash-on-hold view was right, and the view that the March 2027 implied rate would stay pinned below cash was wrong.
postmortems.expression_assessment: Receiving March 2027 Australia at 4.83 versus a 4.85 cash rate was flat-to-negative carry, so the expression did not pay for the wait.
postmortems.timing_assessment: The hold from early October was long enough for a 5 basis point rise from 4.83 to 4.88 to become the exit while the distant 4.60 cash stop never came into play.
postmortems.sizing_assessment: Size converted that small path rise into a realized loss on a receive that started with no carry over cash.
postmortems.lesson: A short-term rate receive entered at or below unchanged cash has no carry cushion, and a far-away cash-regime stop does not contain a few-basis-point path reprice.
postmortems.future_rule: Receive a short-term rate only when the implied rate is materially above unchanged cash so the carry pays for the hold, and do not flatten an existing positive-carry Canada or short-term receive on a sub-5 basis point implied backup from an oil headline while cash policy is unchanged.

causal.original_belief: Receiving Australia March 2027 at 4.83 would work if the implied rate fell, with the trade invalidated only by a break of the 4.60 cash regime or a large persistent path reprice higher.
causal.observed_reality: Cash is still 4.85, the receive was sold at 4.88 versus a 4.83 entry, and the hold from early October to the prior session realized a loss.
causal.assumptions_right: The cash-regime assumption held, because Australia cash stayed at 4.85 and the 4.60 break never printed.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The entry underweighted that a receive struck at 4.83 against 4.85 cash had no positive carry, so a 5 basis point rise to 4.88 could be realized while the cash invalidation stayed far away.
causal.causal_divergence: The loss came from the implied path rising from 4.83 to 4.88, and the fresh March contract near 4.885 versus cash at 4.85 is still only a few basis points of premium.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same early-October information, declining a receive priced through cash, or setting the invalidation on a nearby path reprice rather than on a 4.60 cash break, would have avoided the 4.88 exit.
causal.future_implication: The open Canada March receive still embeds a large premium over unchanged 2.52 cash at a 2.965 fresh mid, while Australia March near 4.885 versus 4.85 cash does not pay enough carry to re-enter.

rate-hawk.thesis: US consumer prices rose 0.4 percent, the two-year is 4.73, and the ten-year is 4.98. Cash funding is 3.88, December futures are 4.28, March 2027 is 4.53, and September 2027 is 4.655, so the US pays stay because the hikes are already the book rather than a new chase. Canada cash at 2.52 against March at 2.965 is the same story in smaller size. September Australia at 4.705 is still 14 basis points under 4.85 cash, so that priced cut is the add.
rate-hawk.invalidation: Remove the September Australia add if that contract makes a new low under 4.705 while cash stays at 4.85 and December futures fall back through 4.165. The US and Canada pays are wrong if September US futures fall back through 4.435 and March Canada through 2.885 without another inflation surprise.

lifecycle.realization_logic: September Australia implied rises from 4.705 back through cash at 4.85 as the priced cut is removed.
lifecycle.catalyst_logic: The 0.4 percent US inflation print is the impulse. Later Australian inflation and policy decisions have to stop validating an easing path.

rates_candidate.rationale: September Australia at 4.705 is still under 4.85 cash, so the path prices a cut after the US strip has already jumped.

spot_candidate.rationale: A higher Australia path would support the Australian dollar at 0.6903, but the mispricing is the September implied rate, not the spot.

expression_memo.rationale: Paying September Australia is the direct expression of a cut that the US inflation print says should not be priced. Spot is the comparison and is not the cleaner line.

stir_policy_path.rationale: Cash is 4.85 and September 2027 is 4.705. The US strip already prices hikes, so the Australia September pay is the path that has not repriced.

two_year.rationale: The US two-year is 4.73 after a 17 basis point rise. Paying it now chases a move that has already printed.

five_year.rationale: The five-year is 4.81. It is the same inflation shock, not a cleaner policy-path pay than September Australia.

swinger.thesis: Australian dollar-kiwi at 1.2266 is still a five-year z-score of 2.34 and the 96th percentile, so the extreme that justified the short from 1.2456 has not closed. The five-day decline and the close beyond the prior range say that extreme is breaking lower. The same 300 million short would be initiated from a flat book here, because a one percent adverse move is about 3 million of shock inside the 100 million limit. Desks cutting the cross reduce crowding. They do not remove the extreme.
swinger.invalidation: The short is invalid if spot reverses back inside the prior range and trades back toward the 1.2456 entry, or if the five-year reading leaves a z-score of 2.34 and the 96th percentile.

harvest_review.remaining_edge_reason: Fresh spot 1.22661 is still a five-year z of 2.34 and the 96th percentile after a 1.2 percent five-day decline and a close beyond the prior 20-session range, so the same 300 million short would be initiated from flat.

performance_reflections.what_happened_vs_expected: The Australian dollar-kiwi short from 1.24556 was expected to work because the pair was a five-year extreme, with an uneven path allowed. It is a material winner at fresh spot 1.22661, but open profit gave back while rank was still first, before the latest five-day decline and the close beyond the prior 20-session range.
performance_reflections.no_new_lesson: The giveback on this Australian dollar-kiwi short was bounded variance around a position that is still a material winner from 1.24556 to 1.22661, and the prior process remains sound because the five-year z is still 2.34 and the 96th percentile was never invalidated by the dip.

causal.original_belief: The cross was rich on a five-year lookback and a spot short would be paid if that extreme mean-reverted, even if the mark path was uneven.
causal.observed_reality: The short is in the money from 1.24556 to fresh spot 1.22661, yet profit gave back before the five-day decline and the break of the prior range. The extreme did not clear: the z-score is still 2.34 and the percentile is still 96.
causal.assumptions_right: The extreme was real, spot was the right expression, and a non-monotonic path did not by itself remove the edge.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The path underweighted how much open profit could be given back while the z-score stayed at 2.34, and how sharply a high-water dip would feel like a process failure.
causal.causal_divergence: The mark retraced part of the gain even though the five-year extreme was still in place, so the profit path and the thesis diverged for a stretch.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same extreme and the same giveback, the book would have stayed short. Flattening the dip would have been a reaction to rank, not to a z-score that had normalized.
causal.future_implication: A high-water wiggle is a prompt to ask whether the same 300 million short would be initiated at the fresh spot. It is not a reason to flatten while the z-score is 2.34, the pair is still the 96th percentile, and the prior range has broken lower.

performance_reflections.what_happened_vs_expected: The Australian dollar-kiwi short was expected to keep extending once it was in the money from the 1.24556 entry. Instead open profit was given back while the book sat second, with fresh spot still 1.22661 versus that entry and only a small step through the 1.22820 book mark.
performance_reflections.no_new_lesson: The giveback is bounded variance around a short that is still in the money, fresh spot 1.22661 versus entry 1.24556, a stall inside the winner and not a reversal through entry. The prior process remains sound because a full-size hold already has to clear a would-initiate test, and that test fails at 1.22661, so the existing harvest rule cuts the line in half.

causal.original_belief: Australia would keep underperforming New Zealand on a tradable spot cross, and the full 20 million short could be held while that move was in motion.
causal.observed_reality: Spot 1.22661 versus entry 1.24556 is still a winner, with the book mark at 1.22820. Open profit was given back while rank was high, and several traders are trimming the same cross.
causal.assumptions_right: The spot cross stayed tradable and was the correct sleeve while New Zealand yields are research-only, and the short from 1.24556 still has directional content.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: Residual downside once the cross was already near the book mark was thinner than the original entry, and rank raised the hurdle to bank open profit and kept full size through the giveback.
causal.causal_divergence: The profit path diverged from the full-size hold because the cross stopped extending while the short thesis from 1.24556 had not broken.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the entry, the book mark, fresh spot still near that mark, and a giveback flag, the same information supports buying back half the short rather than re-litigating a full hold at 1.22661.
causal.future_implication: Full size on this short requires a would-initiate test at the fresh spot. That test fails at 1.22661, so the line is cut to 10 million. Rank is not a reason to add.
